CVE-2026-102927.title: HedgeDoc: Missing validation of incoming permission values on change
CVE-2026-102927.description: HedgeDoc is an open source, real-time collaborative markdown notes application. Prior to 1.11.1, the WebSocket permission handler allows a note owner to store strings outside the supported freely, editable, limited, locked, protected, and private permission values. The viewing and editing checks handle only known values and can otherwise fall through to permissive behavior, making a note readable or writable more broadly than intended. SQLite deployments can persist the invalid value because the database column does not strictly enforce the set, while MySQL and PostgreSQL reject the database update but can leave the in-memory note state inconsistent for connected users until reload or cache eviction. Exploitation requires the note owner to intentionally submit an invalid permission value, and the owner could already choose a legitimate permissive setting, which limits the practical security impact. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.1.

CVE-2026-124286.title: TLS 1.2 Client Completes Handshake Without a Server Certificate
CVE-2026-124286.description:
Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability in Erlang OTP ssl (ssl_handshake module) allows an on-path attacker to impersonate any server to a TLS 1.2 or DTLS client.

When a server sends no Certificate message and a ServerKeyExchange without a signature, ssl_handshake:decode_server_key/3 reports the signature algorithm as anon, and ssl_handshake:verify_signature/5 returns true for anon without a public key. The client does not require a certificate for a certificate-authenticated key exchange, so the handshake completes for the ecdhe_rsa, ecdhe_ecdsa, dhe_rsa and dhe_dss key exchanges with a cipher suite the client offered. Certificate path validation, verify_fun and the hostname check do not run, and ssl:connect/3 returns {ok, Socket} with {verify, verify_peer} set. The TLS 1.3 client is not affected.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.14, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.0.3, corresponding to ssl from 5.3.4 before 11.2.12.10, 11.6.0.8, and 11.7.3.

CVE-2026-129784.title: Insecure deserializaiton in the httpx Ruby gem via unsafe Oj object-mode
CVE-2026-129784.description: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

CVE-2026-133743.description:
The fix for CVE-2026-123339 (GHSA-wg5q-m2ww-f3c9) restores the router context of the main request after an inline fragment, but the cause of that issue is still there. A page can render an inline fragment with render() in Twig, or with an ESI tag when no gateway cache is used. While the fragment runs, SubRequestHandler adds 127.0.0.1 to the trusted proxies of every request. Code that reads the main request during that time trusts its X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded headers if the main request came from 127.0.0.1.

- asset() takes the base path and the scheme of the main request. Request::getBasePath() keeps its first result, so when it's first computed inside the fragment, the later asset() calls of the page return such URLs too.

CVE-2026-69158.title: Atomic Server: Unauthenticated full-response SSRF in Atomic-Server /bookmark endpoint
CVE-2026-69158.description: Atomic Server is an open source headless CMS and real-time database. Prior to 0.40.3, unauthenticated requests to /bookmark can supply a url that server/src/plugins/bookmark.rs passes through fetch_data to fetch_body. Endpoint dispatch in lib/src/db.rs invokes the handler before check_read, and lib/src/client/helpers.rs previously checked only that the URL began with HTTP, without restricting loopback, private, link-local, DNS-rebinding, or redirect targets. The handler reflects fetched content in returned resource fields, making this a full-response server-side request forgery that can expose internal services and plain-GET cloud metadata. The short request timeout limits slow targets, and metadata services requiring a separate token request are outside the demonstrated GET-only path. This issue is fixed in version 0.40.3.

CVE-2026-78189.title: WebDyne versions from 3.007 before 3.022 for Perl execute .psp files outside the document root via path traversal in the PSGI API route fallback
CVE-2026-78189.description:
WebDyne versions from 3.007 before 3.022 for Perl execute .psp files outside the document root via path traversal in the PSGI API route fallback.

When a request matches no file, the PSGI handler retries it as an API route through api_filename. That keeps .. segments in the request path and only checks that the joined path starts with the document root, which a request for /../private passes.

A remote attacker can run the embedded Perl in any .psp file the server can read, such as one uploaded to a directory outside the document root.

CVE-2026-92189.title: Quest Foglight for Databases writeTopologySectionToFile External Control of File Path Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
CVE-2026-92189.description:
Quest Foglight for Databases writeTopologySectionToFile External Control of File Path Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of Quest Foglight for Databases. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the writeTopologySectionToFile method. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-29169.

CVE-2026-99405.title: xfs: abort dirtree repair if the live update hook dies
CVE-2026-99405.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: abort dirtree repair if the live update hook dies

LOLLM notices that if the live update hook for the directory tree repair
code hits an error, it will set dl->aborted and stops working. If the
repair code ever sees that condition, it ought to bail out immediately
instead of continuing with obsolete data.

CVE-2026-99470.title: media: cx23885: unregister DVB bus when SP2 CI setup fails
CVE-2026-99470.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: cx23885: unregister DVB bus when SP2 CI setup fails

The DVBSKY S950C, DVBSKY T980C and TechnoTrend CT2-4500 CI paths register
the DVB bus before attaching their SP2 CI client. If that client cannot be
created, bound, or pinned, the current error path removes the I2C frontend
components and only deallocates the frontend list, leaving the registered
DVB adapter behind. Removing an I2C demod before unregistering the DVB bus
can also expose the use-after-free ordering fixed for the normal remove
path.

Unregister the DVB bus immediately when SP2 CI setup fails, before the
existing I2C client cleanup. The bus helper empties the frontend list, so
the later frontend deallocation has nothing left to release. Keep failures
from vb2_dvb_register_bus() on the existing cleanup path. Also release an
unbound SP2 client and propagate the actual I2C creation or CI registration
error.

CVE-2026-99614.title: drm/nouveau/nvkm: clear use.enabled when subdev init fails
CVE-2026-99614.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/nouveau/nvkm: clear use.enabled when subdev init fails

On Kepler boards without the video decode falcon firmware installed
(msvld/mspdec/msppp), every other VA-API decode attempt binds to an
engine with no ucode loaded. The submitted work never completes, which
leads to a context switch timeout, a channel recovery that cannot reset
the engine, and eviction waits on fences that never signal. The process
ends up stuck in D state, or killed by SIGBUS when it touches a buffer
evicted after the wait times out:

msvld: unable to load firmware data
msvld: init failed, -19
fifo: SCHED_ERROR 0a [CTXSW_TIMEOUT]
vo[5444]: channel 14 killed!
WARNING: drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nvkm/engine/fifo/runl.c:117 at nvkm_runl_rc+0x2a4/0x3b0 [nouveau]
[TTM] Buffer eviction failed
WARNING: drivers/gpu/drm/nouveau/nouveau_bo.c:1092 at nouveau_bo_move_ntfy.part.0+0x9b/0x100 [nouveau]
